paragraphs: Robb Report identifies Olson Kundig as the designer of this Kona Coast home. Rather than gathering every room beneath one large roof, the project distributes its accommodation across smaller structures. We like the resulting emphasis on the journey between rooms: gardens become part of the architectural experience, rather than decoration around its edges.

The publication describes a screened entrance and a route that eventually brings the ocean into view. That progression gives the setting time to register. For us, it is a persuasive alternative to revealing everything at once, especially where the surrounding volcanic terrain already offers such a strong visual presence.

The reported arrangement separates the owners’ accommodation from the communal rooms and gives bedrooms their own outdoor areas. A sheltered connection maintains continuity between buildings. The appeal is the choice this offers: gathering together need not mean surrendering quieter places to withdraw, and outdoor bathing becomes part of that more private experience.
A close reading of the ground

Basalt underfoot, substantial concrete surfaces and timber details connect the material palette to the setting described by Robb Report. Shade is another design ingredient, created through projecting roofs. We love the attention to these everyday encounters with light, texture and shelter; spectacular scenery alone would be a less interesting architectural story.
